newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES COACH SMITH ATTACKS CRITICS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES COACH SMITH ATTACKS CRITICS.

text.p: Australia rugby union coach Greg Smith has labelled critics of his side's performance during their recently unbeaten European tour as "treacherous and traitorous".

Smith singled out his predecessor Bob Dwyer for particular attention, claiming the England-based coach was negative in his comments about Australian rugby because he still wanted the national team job.
"I was Captain Rats steering the ship onto the rocks all the time -- it's just insane," Smith told Sydney's Daily Telegraph newspaper on Wednesday.
The Wallabies returned to Australia on Monday after an unbeaten 12-match tour of Italy, Britain and Ireland.
Australia won all four test matches against Italy, Ireland, Scotland and Wales but their performances on tour received mixed reviews from media commentators, including Dwyer.
"The thing is that he (Dwyer) is just so transparent...He's completely committed to the negative," Smith said.
"At the end of the day it becomes a bit of a joke and you think he can't be serious," he said.

During the tour several reports appeared in the Australian media suggesting Smith's job would be on the line if results went against them. He described the unnamed people who supposedly plotted against him as "pathetic".

"They are treacherous and traitorous people who basically have no regard for any sort of nationalistic feeling," Smith said. "All they care about are their own grotty little agendas and the sooner Australian rugby gets rid of them the better we will all be."
Dwyer, who guided Australia to success in the 1991 World Cup, was replaced after he failed to repeat the achievement in South Africa last year.
Smith said the Wallabies won 73 percent of their games in 1996, compared to a record of 50 percent in the 1995 season.
Australia finished bottom of the southern hemisphere Tri-Nation series involving New Zealand and South Africa in 1996 after crashing to a record 43-6 defeat against the All Blacks in Wellington.
